html:
Kyichu Lhakhang is a small temple in the Paro valley of Bhutan, said to have been built in the 7th century by the Tibetan king Songtsen Gampo, which would make it one of the oldest in the country.

Legend says the king built 108 temples in one day to pin down a giant demoness lying across Tibet and the Himalaya, and Kyichu held down her left foot. Jampa Lhakhang in Bumthang is said to be another of the set.

Whatever its exact age, the temple marks the coming of Buddhism from Tibet to the valleys that became Bhutan. The teacher Padmasambhava, who is said to have visited a century later, is remembered at nearby Paro Taktsang. Kyichu is still a living temple, and the royal family has added shrines to it in modern times.
